text.p: DuPont Co Chief Financial officer Kurt Landgraf said the firm would probably "significantly" expand production capacity of specialty fibers, particularly its Lycra brand spandex.

"Our specialty fiber products, especially Lycra, are doing extraordinarly well on a global basis, to the point that we will probably expanding capacity significantly to meet worldwide demand," Landgraf told a telephone news conference.
Landgraf said DuPont's board had not yet approved the expansion plans and he could not comment in detail. "We will be announcing these things in the relative near future," he said.

Increased earnings for Lycra and well as Dacron polyester and nonwoven fibers helped boost DuPont's second-quarter fiber-segment earnings 18 percent from a year earlier, to $245 million, DuPont said earlier.

The Dacron business has in the last year experienced a "very important" turnaround in earnings after four or five years of losses, Landgraf said. This was achieved by improved market share and cost cuts, he said.
He also said DuPont had recently increased capacity in nylon after nearing capacity limits.
Landgraf said high-growth specialty fibers, including Lycra, Kevlar, Tyvek, and spandex accounted for two-thirds of the fiber segment earnings in the second quarter 1997.
